findings.evidence: The _LocationTap branch sets rec.refusal_code=HOST_NON_ENGLISH, but _get returns FetchResult(rec) with no refused_url, so ResearchJob._note_blocked keys the site on record.requested_url. Probe: ResearchJob with urls a.example and b.example, both 302 -> http://ｐａｙｐａｌ.com/, gives blocked_non_english=2; the same job with Location http://%D1%80aypal.com/ (refused via check_url at the next hop, refused_url set) gives 1. The note then says 'did not open 2 sites' for one site.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry the joined raw Location to FetchResult.refused_url (e.g. store it on rec or return it from _exchange) when the tap check refuses it.
findings.title: httpx-rejected redirect refusal is counted under the redirecting site, not the refused target (per-site count R1-02 inexact)

findings.evidence: unquote(host) uses errors='replace', so http://%FF.com/ and http://a%E2%80%8B.com/ change from HOST_INVALID to HOST_NON_ENGLISH (differential fuzz: all 30,842 differences were HOST_INVALID->HOST_NON_ENGLISH, none newly allowed). The D33 text then calls them non-English letters and suggests opening them in a browser, which cannot open them either. Still refused, so cosmetic only.
findings.suggested_fix: Return HOST_NON_ENGLISH only when the decoded host is valid UTF-8 containing letters (e.g. unquote(host, errors='strict') plus a str.isalpha check on the non-ASCII characters); otherwise keep HOST_INVALID.
findings.title: Percent escapes decoding to non-letters (invalid UTF-8, zero-width, NBSP) are reported as 'non-English letters' and the user is told to open them in a browser
